     2→
     3→> This document teaches an AI agent about the Ableton Live Set file format,
     4→> music production concepts relevant to giving feedback, and common patterns
     5→> to look for when analyzing projects.
     6→
     7→---
     8→
     9→## ALS File Format
    10→
    11→### Physical Format
    12→- `.als` files are **gzip-compressed XML** (or sometimes uncompressed XML — Ableton reads both)
    13→- `.adg` files (device groups/racks) use the same format
    14→- `.alc` files (clips) use the same format
    15→- XML is verbose: a simple project is ~2K lines, a real project is 10K–200K+ lines
    16→- Decompress: `gzip -cd song.als > song.xml` or Python's `gzip.open()`
    17→
    18→### XML Hierarchy (Ableton 11/12)
    19→```
    20→<Ableton MajorVersion="5" MinorVersion="11.x.x" Creator="Ableton Live 11...">
    21→  <LiveSet>
    22→    <Tempo>                         # Project tempo (automation points if automated)
    23→    <TimeSignature>                 # Time signature
    24→    <Locators>                      # Arrangement markers/locators
    25→    <Tracks>                        # All tracks
    26→      <AudioTrack Id="N">           # Audio track
    27→      <MidiTrack Id="N">            # MIDI track
    28→      <GroupTrack Id="N">           # Group/folder track
    29→      <ReturnTrack Id="N">          # Return/bus track
    30→      | <Name><UserName Value="..."/></Name>
    31→      | <Color Value="N"/>          # Track color (integer index)
    32→      | <TrackGroupId Value="N"/>   # Parent group (-1 if none)
    33→      | <DeviceChain>               # THE BIG ONE — contains everything
    34→      |   <AutomationLanes>         # Automation data
    35→      |   <MainSequencer>           # Arrangement view clips
    36→      |   |   <ClipSlotList>        # Session view clip slots
    37→      |   |   <Sample>              # (AudioTrack) Audio clip reference
    38→      |   |   <ArrangerAutomation>  # Arrangement clip envelopes
    39→      |   <MidiControllers>         # (MidiTrack only) MIDI CC data
    40→      |   <Mixer>                   # Volume, pan, sends, crossfade
    41→      |   |   <Volume><Manual Value="0.85"/></Volume>   # 0.0–1.0
    42→      |   |   <Pan><Manual Value="0"/></Pan>             # -1.0 to 1.0
    43→      |   |   <Sends>               # Send levels to return tracks
    44→      |   |   <Speaker Value="true"/>  # Track on/off
    45→      |   <DeviceChain>             # Nested devices (instruments, effects)
    46→      |   |   <Devices>
    47→      |   |     <PluginDevice>      # VST/AU plugin
    48→      |   |     <Eq8>               # Ableton EQ Eight
    49→      |   |     <Compressor2>       # Ableton Compressor
    50→      |   |     <AutoFilter>        # Ableton Auto Filter
    51→      |   |     <InstrumentGroupDevice> # Instrument Rack
    52→      |   |     <AudioEffectGroupDevice> # Audio Effect Rack
    53→      |   |     ...
    54→    <MasterTrack>                   # Master channel
    55→    <PreHearTrack>                  # Cue/preview channel
    56→    <Transport>                     # Play/stop/loop state
    57→    <ViewData>                      # UI state (zoom, scroll, selected track)
    58→    <Scenes>                        # Session view scenes
    59→```
    60→
    61→### Key Element Patterns
    62→
    63→**Track identification:**
    64→```xml
    65→<MidiTrack Id="4">
    66→  <Name><UserName Value="Lead Synth"/><EffectiveName Value="Lead Synth"/></Name>
    67→  <Color Value="24"/>
    68→  <TrackGroupId Value="2"/>  <!-- belongs to group track Id=2 -->
    69→```
    70→
    71→**MIDI clip with notes:**
    72→```xml
    73→<MidiClip Id="0" Time="0">
    74→  <Name Value="intro melody"/>
    75→  <CurrentStart Value="0"/>
    76→  <CurrentEnd Value="16"/>       <!-- length in beats -->
    77→  <Loop>
    78→    <LoopStart Value="0"/>
    79→    <LoopEnd Value="16"/>
    80→    <StartRelative Value="0"/>
    81→    <LoopOn Value="true"/>
    82→  </Loop>
    83→  <Notes>
    84→    <KeyTracks>
    85→      <KeyTrack Id="0">
    86→        <MidiKey Value="60"/>    <!-- MIDI note number (60 = C3) -->
    87→        <Notes>
    88→          <MidiNoteEvent Time="0" Duration="0.5" Velocity="100" .../>
    89→          <MidiNoteEvent Time="2" Duration="1.0" Velocity="80" .../>
    90→```
    91→
    92→**Audio clip with sample reference:**
    93→```xml
    94→<AudioClip Id="0" Time="0">
    95→  <SampleRef>
    96→    <FileRef>
    97→      <RelativePath Value="Samples/..."/>
    98→      <Path Value="/absolute/path/to/sample.wav"/>
    99→      <Type Value="1"/>  <!-- 1=file exists -->
   100→    </FileRef>
   101→  </SampleRef>
   102→  <WarpMode

    18→---
    19→
    20→## Setup
    21→
    22→### 1. Place the toolkit in your project or a central location
    23→```bash
    24→# Option A: Central location (works across all Ableton projects)
    25→cp -r als_tools/ ~/tools/als_tools/
    26→
    27→# Option B: Inside an Ableton project
    28→cp -r als_tools/ /path/to/my-ableton-project/als_tools/
    29→```
    30→
    31→### 2. Ensure Claude Code can access it
    32→When starting a Claude Code session, make sure the working directory contains or can reach the `als_tools/` package. No external dependencies needed — it uses only Python standard library (`gzip`, `xml.etree.ElementTree`, `json`, `pathlib`).
    33→
    34→### 3. Provide the skill file
    35→Copy `docs/ableton-skill.md` into your Claude Code skills directory, or reference it in your CLAUDE.md:
    36→```markdown
    37→For Ableton domain knowledge, read docs/ableton-skill.md before analyzing any .als file.

    68→
    69→### Workflow 2: Deep Dive on Specific Aspect

    71→```

    73→
    74→python -m als_tools.extract "/path/to/song.als" --mixer

    76→
    77→Analyze the gain staging across all tracks. Are any tracks too hot?

    81→
    82→### Workflow 3: MIDI Analysis

    84→```
    85→python -m als_tools.extract "/path/to/song.als" --midi-notes
    86→
    87→Analyze the MIDI data. Look for:
    88→- Velocity patterns (are they static/robotic or dynamic?)

    90→- Pitch range and key estimation
    91→- Any clips that might benefit from humanization
    92→```
    93→
    94→### Workflow 4: Sample Health Check
    95→

     2→
     3→## What This Is
     4→A Python toolkit that lets Claude Code read, analyze, and suggest edits to Ableton Live projects (.als files). ALS files are gzip-compressed XML — this project provides extraction, summarization, and safe editing tools.
     5→
     6→## Quick Start
     7→```bash
     8→# Parse and summarize a Live Set
     9→python als_tools/summarize.py /path/to/project/song.als
    10→
    11→# Extract specific data
    12→python als_tools/extract.py /path/to/song.als --tracks       # Track list with devices
    13→python als_tools/extract.py /path/to/song.als --clips         # All clips (MIDI + audio)
    14→python als_tools/extract.py /path/to/song.als --mixer         # Mixer settings (vol, pan, sends)
    15→python als_tools/extract.py /path/to/song.als --routing       # I/O routing
    16→python als_tools/extract.py /path/to/song.als --devices       # Full device chain dump
    17→python als_tools/extract.py /path/to/song.als --midi-notes    # MIDI note data per clip
    18→python als_tools/extract.py /path/to/song.als --tempo         # Tempo, time sig, locators
    19→
    20→# Edit a Live Set (always creates a backup first)
    21→python als_tools/edit.py /path/to/song.als --rename-track 3 "Bass Reese"
    22→python als_tools/edit.py /path/to/song.als --set-volume 3 0.75
    23→python als_tools/edit.py /path/to/song.als --set-color 3 24
    24→python als_tools/edit.py /path/to/song.als --set-tempo 174
    25→```
    26→
    27→## Critical Rules
    28→- **ALWAYS back up before editing.** The edit tool does this automatically, but verify.
    29→- **Ableton reads uncompressed XML** if the file has an .als extension. So we save edits as uncompressed XML (simpler, no risk of gzip corruption).
    30→- **NEVER modify VST/AU preset buffers** — the hex data is opaque and fragile.
    31→- **NEVER reorder XML elements** — Ableton may depend on element ordering.
    32→- **Test edits by opening the file in Ableton** — there is no schema validator.
    33→
    34→## Project Structure
    35→```
    36→als_tools/
    37→  parser.py       # Core ALS parser (gzip decompress → XML tree)
    38→  summarize.py    # Produces a human-readable project summary
    39→  extract.py      # Targeted extraction (tracks, clips, mixer, etc.)
    40→  edit.py          # Safe editing operations with backup
    41→  models.py        # Dataclasses representing ALS structures
    42→  xml_paths.py     # XPath constants for ALS XML navigation
    43→```
    44→
    45→## For Ableton domain knowledge, see `docs/ableton-skill.md`
    46→'}]}

{'role': 'user', 'content': [{'tool_use_id': 'toolu_01RFV1T7qurV8sgK39j6puR3', 'type': 'tool_result', 'content': '     1→"""
     2→Core parser for Ableton Live Set (.als) files.
     3→
     4→ALS files are gzip-compressed XML. Ableton also reads uncompressed XML
     5→with .als extension, so we save edits as uncompressed XML for safety.
     6→"""
     7→
     8→import gzip
     9→import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
    10→from pathlib import Path
    11→
    12→
    13→def load_als(path: str | Path) -> ET.ElementTree:
    14→    """Load an ALS file and return the parsed XML ElementTree.
    15→    
    16→    Handles both gzip-compressed and uncompressed .als files.
    17→    """
    18→    path = Path(path)
    19→    if not path.exists():
    20→        raise FileNotFoundError(f"ALS file not found: {path}")
    21→    
    22→    # Try gzip first (most common), fall back to plain XML
    23→    try:
    24→        with gzip.open(path, "rb") as f:
    25→            raw = f.read()
    26→    except gzip.BadGzipFile:
    27→        with open(path, "rb") as f:
    28→            raw = f.read()
    29→    
    30→    root = ET.fromstring(raw)
    31→    return ET.ElementTree(root)
    32→
    33→
    34→def save_als(tree: ET.ElementTree, path: str | Path, compress: bool = False):
    35→    """Save an ElementTree back to an ALS file.
    36→    
    37→    By default saves as uncompressed XML (Ableton reads both).
    38→    Set compress=True for gzip output.
    39→    """
    40→    path = Path(path)
    41→    
    42→    xml_bytes = ET.tostring(tree.getroot(), encoding="UTF-8", xml_declaration=True)
    43→    
    44→    if compress:
    45→        with gzip.open(path, "wb") as f:
    46→            f.write(xml_bytes)
    47→    else:
    48→        with open(path, "wb") as f:
    49→            f.write(xml_bytes)
    50→
    51→
    52→def get_ableton_version(tree: ET.ElementTree) -> dict:
    53→    """Extract Ableton version info from the root element."""
    54→    root = tree.getroot()
    55→    return {
    56→        "major_version": root.get("MajorVersion", "?"),
    57→        "minor_version": root.get("MinorVersion", "?"),
    58→        "creator": root.get("Creator", "?"),
    59→        "revision": root.get("Revision", "?"),
    60→    }
    61→
    62→
    63→def get_all_tracks(tree: ET.ElementTree) -> list[ET.Element]:
    64→    """Get all track elements in document order."""
    65→    from . import xml_paths as xp
    66→    
    67→    tracks = []
    68→    for xpath in xp.ALL_TRACKS:
    69→        tracks.extend(tree.findall(xpath))
    70→    
    71→    # Sort by Id attribute to preserve document order
    72→    tracks.sort(key=lambda t: int(t.get("Id", 0)))
    73→    return tracks
    74→
    75→
    76→def get_track_type(track: ET.Element) -> str:
    77→    """Return the track type as a string."""
    78→    tag = track.tag
    79→    type_map = {
    80→        "AudioTrack": "audio",
    81→        "MidiTrack": "midi",
    82→        "GroupTrack": "group",
    83→        "ReturnTrack": "return",
    84→    }
    85→    return type_map.get(tag, "unknown")
    86→'}]}

text_parts: Good context. Let me put together the architect brief with everything they'll need — current state, vision, constraints, and the M4L question.

Done. The brief is at `ARCHITECT_BRIEF.md`. Here's what it covers:

**Current state** — full inventory of what the prototype can and can't do today.

**Target capabilities** in three tiers (must/should/nice-to-have), from MIDI clip creation through template generation.

**Five key design questions** the architect needs to resolve:

1. **File-based vs. M4L vs. hybrid** — includes a trade-off table. The M4L approach gives real-time interaction but the Live API has gaps (limited arrangement access). File-based gives full XML control but requires reload. A hybrid could be the sweet spot.
2. **MIDI generation strategy** — minimum valid clip XML, music theory layer, pattern library
3. **Device parameter mapping** — static tables vs. dynamic parsing for native device params
4. **Safety/validation** — no ALS schema exists, so how do we verify edits?
5. **Integration layer** — Claude Code skill vs. MCP server vs. both

**Constraints** are locked in: Ableton 11+ only, Python stdlib only, macOS primary, safety-first.

You can hand this file (plus the `als-reader/` directory for code context) to your architect. Want me to adjust anything in the brief?
